name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3259
preamble: Joshua Kosman and Henri Picciotto Share Copy Link Facebook X (Twitter) Bluesky Pocket Email October 31, 2012 This article appears in the November 19, 2012 issue.

clue.text: Snatch, using every element as needed in whatever way possible

blocks.clueFragment: Snatch, using every element as needed
blocks.note: surface reading: grab what you can, using whatever comes to hand
setter's reading: the phrase is spelt entirely from chemical symbols, calcium, technetium, hydrogen, arsenic and nitrogen among them

explanation.surface: A thief grabbing loot by any means at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: CATCH-AS-CATCH-CAN splits into Ca Tc H As Ca Tc H Ca N, every piece a chemical symbol, and the first word means snatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for doing something by any available method, without a plan or rules.

clue.text: You are reading one excerpt from Bicycle Week…

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece lifted out of a longer text, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A reader is handed a passage from a magazine's cycling issue.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEW is an old spelling of clue, and what you are reading right now is a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Clew is an archaic variant spelling of clue, the very thing a solver is reading.

clue.text: …the excerpt initially gets you

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of excerpt

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a passage from the magazine wins you over.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie this to 1-down, but the two clues are solved separately; THEE is the old object form of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic singular object pronoun, used where modern English says you.

clue.text: On the rebound, Ohio State struggling in a position of anxiety

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
a team struggling is in disarray, so the letters of the next word are put out of order

blocks.note: OH is the postal abbreviation for Ohio
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ohio State's basketball team losing the battle for rebounds, which leaves the coach anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Ohio State is a university with a famous sports program, but here the two words are split: Ohio's abbreviation turns round and State is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the hot seat is an idiom for facing pressure or scrutiny, an uncomfortable spot to be in.

clue.text: Pipe lifted under spring for someone like Picasso

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upside down, so it reads from bottom to top
in a down entry, a piece placed under another comes after it

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
a drain is a pipe carrying waste water

explanation.surface: A plumbing job in springtime, oddly ending with a famous painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso was born in Málaga, so he is an example of a person from Spain.

clue.text: Erase outside of a bluebonnet, for instance

indicators.note: one word goes outside the next, wrapping round it

blocks.note: to annul is to cancel or wipe out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rubbing out the outline of a flower in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: The bluebonnet is a blue lupine, the state flower of Texas, which grows from seed each year.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a plant that completes its life cycle in one year, as the Texas bluebonnet does.

clue.text: Stingier imitator of a revolutionary

indicators.note: the imitator belongs to the revolutionary, so it is attached to him, following his name

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
an aper is one who apes, or copies

explanation.surface: Someone copying a radical is meaner with money than the original.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheaper describes someone less willing to spend, the comparative of tight-fisted.

clue.text: Brad follows antiwar clergyman for a cigarette

indicators.note: the first named piece comes after the second, so the order is swapped

blocks.note: William Sloane Coffin, Yale chaplain and Vietnam War protester
a brad is a small thin nail

explanation.surface: Someone named Brad trailing a peace-campaigning minister, hoping to cadge a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Brad looks like a man's name, but it is a small nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffin nail is old slang for a cigarette, since each one is said to bring death closer.

clue.text: Chant-22: experimental film starring Greta Garbo

indicators.note: experimental work tries new arrangements, so the letters before it are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
the number stands for the answer to 22-down

explanation.surface: An avant-garde project, pointedly numbered like Catch-22, built around a Garbo performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Chant-22 mimics the title Catch-22, but 22 is a cross-reference to the barnyard noise at 22-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninotchka is the 1939 Lubitsch comedy in which Greta Garbo plays a Soviet envoy, billed with the line Garbo laughs.

clue.text: Indeed, riding in a subway on the West Side of Manhattan produces vision fatigue

indicators.note: a passenger riding in a train is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.clueFragment: a subway on the West Side of Manhattan
blocks.note: the E train runs down Eighth Avenue on Manhattan's West Side
yes affirms, just as indeed does

explanation.surface: A New Yorker complaining that reading on the subway tires the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: New York subway services are named by single letters or digits, so a particular line is clued by its route.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is the tiredness and discomfort of eyes overworked by reading or screens.

clue.text: In Mexico, the end is otherworldly

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the, Spanish being Mexico's language
fin is the Spanish word for end, and also an English word for the close of a film

explanation.surface: A traveller in Mexico finds the finish of a journey strangely unreal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, so suggesting fairyland, a magical realm beyond the everyday.

clue.text: Remarkably, I'm a pencil dot!

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters that follow are scrambled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tiny mark on paper boasting about its own importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the description: the dot you pencil between whole number and fraction speaks up.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal point is literally a dot written with a pencil, small but changing a number's value remarkably.

clue.text: Native blood types in (contained by) Riga, the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: the bracketed phrase spells out that the small word goes inside the place name
a capital letter is the first one, so only the opening of the country's name is kept

blocks.note: AB and O are two blood types
taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of Latvia

explanation.surface: A note on the blood groups found among people native to Riga, Latvia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word in goes inside RIGA, giving RIGINA, with the blood types in front and the L after.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal means indigenous, belonging to a place from the earliest times.

clue.text: Mafiosi multiply the head of ten-legged creatures twentyfold

indicators.note: the opening letter is read as a Roman numeral and swapped for the numeral worth that many times more

blocks.note: L is the Roman 50, and twenty times 50 is 1000, the Roman M
lobsters are decapods, with ten legs

explanation.surface: Gangsters ordering a huge seafood feast, twenty times more than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of the crustaceans is a Roman numeral; raised twentyfold it becomes M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mafiosi are members of the Mafia, organised criminals, so gangsters.

clue.text: Michigan gang hanging around to steal local beer

indicators.note: a group hanging around something surrounds it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan
a crew is a gang
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A Detroit gang loitering about, planning to lift beer from a nearby brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: CREW goes round ROB, after the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbrew is beer from a small independent brewery, typically sold in its neighbourhood.

clue.text: Bush originally left part of government for a farm

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter of the name is used
left means departed, so that letter goes away from the phrase that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of Bush
the executive, legislature and judiciary are the branches of US government

explanation.surface: George W. Bush quitting Washington politics to retire to his Texas spread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush did own a ranch in Crawford, Texas, which makes the surface ring true.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in the American West.

clue.text: Rejected part of satire if I'd omitted an adjective, perhaps

indicators.note: only a portion of the phrase that follows is used, sitting across its words
something rejected is sent back, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: the run from the end of the first word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: An editor cutting a bit of a satire because a describing word went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the last letters of satire through I'd and the first two of omitted, then turn them round.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a modifier qualifies another word, and an adjective qualifying a noun is a typical example.

clue.text: Islander's taxi circumventing Rhode Island

indicators.note: to circumvent is literally to go round, so one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: An island-dweller's cab driving around the smallest US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for is, linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are an indigenous people of the Lesser Antilles, so a Carib is an islander of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Show disapproval of Violet around New Jersey rocker

indicators.note: the jeer goes around the state abbreviation, enclosing it

blocks.note: to boo is to show disapproval
NJ is the postal abbreviation for New Jersey
Vi is the short form of the name Violet

explanation.surface: A heckler jeering a woman called Violet, who is a hard-rocking Jersey musician.
explanation.walkthrough: New Jersey looks like part of the definition, and fits it, but it supplies NJ; the band is from Sayreville, New Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon Jovi is the arena-rock band led by Jon Bon Jovi, and also his own stage name.

clue.text: Somalian marred painting

indicators.note: something marred is damaged and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A vandal from Somalia defacing an artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is perhaps the most famous painting in the world.

clue.text: Mollusk: B

blocks.note: what the clue shows is one letter B, standing by itself with nothing else, described in three words

explanation.walkthrough: Describe the lone letter after the colon in words: a B, by itself, all on its own, which reads as the shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail prized for its meat and the mother-of-pearl lining its shell.

clue.text: Immobilize BMW, mostly, with string running back through it

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter is dropped
running back means heading in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards
something running through another lies inside it

blocks.note: the German car maker's name, as written
a lace is a string, as in a shoelace

explanation.surface: Disabling a car by threading cord backwards through its works.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten BMW to BM, then put the turned-round string between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm is to leave a sailing ship motionless for lack of wind, so to bring it to a halt.

clue.text: What you might hear in church: "Liver, kidneys, pancreas…"

definitions.text: What you might hear in church

blocks.clueFragment: What you might hear in church
blocks.note: first meaning: a concert on the pipe instrument at the front of the church
second meaning: a recital is a listing, and these are body parts being recited in a row

explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words sound like a sermon or hymn, but they are just a recitation of body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ recital is a performance on a church organ, and also, punningly, a list of internal organs recited aloud.

clue.text: Barnyard sound: beginning of ominous sign

indicators.note: beginning of keeps just the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first letter of ominous
to ink a contract is to sign it

explanation.surface: A noise from the farmyard heard as a portent of doom.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunt a pig makes, a typical noise in a farmyard.

clue.text: Young man, losing face, is blue

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so losing it means the word gives up its opening letter

blocks.note: Cy Young was a celebrated baseball pitcher, so Young's first name stands for it
the word man with its first letter dropped

explanation.surface: A sad youth whose looks have been lost is feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young man' reads as one phrase meaning a youth, but it splits: Cy Young is the pitcher after whom baseball's annual pitching award is named, and 'man, losing face' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printing primaries, so it is a shade of blue.

clue.text: Drummer's circles

blocks.note: two kinds of circle: a ring, and the round letter O

explanation.walkthrough: Drummer's reads as a possessive, but the apostrophe s is is; the circles are a ring and an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringo Starr played drums for the Beatles, the most famous drummer in pop.

clue.text: is no amity, unfortunately!

indicators.note: things turning out unfortunately go wrong, so the letters before it are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A rueful remark that friendship is absent between two parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts mid-sentence: the missing subject is the answer, and the whole clue is both its definition and its anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is hostility, the very opposite of friendly goodwill.

clue.text: Director's testament: "I am completely worn out by family"

indicators.note: by means beside, so the last piece is set next to the rest

blocks.note: a last will and testament
taken as written
fried is slang for utterly exhausted
kin are family

explanation.surface: A film director's last statement complaining that relatives have exhausted him.
explanation.walkthrough: Director's testament sounds like a single idea; the apostrophe s is is, and testament starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: William Friedkin was the American filmmaker behind The French Connection and The Exorcist.
